    "E1.1"
  ],
  "reasons": [
    "Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative forgone.",
    "The available mutually exclusive alternatives give Rs 0 (house-safe), Rs 10,000 (bank-2 at 5%), and Rs 20,000 (bank-1 at 10%).",
    "The maximum forgone return among the alternatives is Rs 20,000 from bank-1."
  ],
  "syllabus_chapter": "Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition",
  "syllabus_topic": "Profit maximization and opportunity cost",
  "syllabus_entitlement": true,
  "presentation_ready": true,
  "question_type_match": true,
  "principle_applicability": "excerpt_required",
  "decisive_principle_in_excerpts": true,
  "answer_conditions": [
    {
      "condition": "Total invested funds equal Rs 2,00,000",
      "status": "explicit",
      "alters_key_if_changed": true,
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    },
    {
      "condition": "The alternatives are mutually exclusive and only one can be chosen",
      "status": "explicit",
      "alters_key_if_changed": true,
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    },
    {
      "condition": "Opportunity cost is measured by the forgone return of the best alternative activity",
      "status": "convention",
      "alters_key_if_changed": true,
      "convention_evidence_ids": [
        "E1.1"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "option_challenges": [
    {
      "option": "B",
      "strongest_reading": "The opportunity cost is taken from the inferior bank return (bank-2 at 5% of Rs 2,00,000).",
      "correct_under_reading": false,
      "reading_status": "contradicts_stem",
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    },
    {
      "option": "C",
      "strongest_reading": "The opportunity cost is calculated by summing the forgone returns of bank-1 and bank-2.",
      "correct_under_reading": false,
      "reading_status": "contradicts_stem",
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    },
    {
      "option": "D",
      "strongest_reading": "The opportunity cost is taken from the zero return alternative of keeping cash in a safe.",
      "correct_under_reading": false,
      "reading_status": "contradicts_stem",
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    }
  ],
  "blocking_defects": [],
  "style_notes": [],
  "cuet_fit": {
    "criteria": {
      "syllabus_objective": {
        "level": 3,
        "evidence": "Directly applies the definition and calculation of opportunity cost in producer theory."
      },
      "format_authenticity": {
        "level": 3,
        "evidence": "Matches standard CUET numerical calculation items."
      },
      "level_calibration": {
        "level": 3,
        "evidence": "Standard single-step calculation based on NCERT textbook illustration."
      },
      "discrimination_value": {
        "level": 3,
        "evidence": "Distractors target common errors: summing returns or selecting the non-optimal alternative."
      }
    },
    "reasoning_steps": 2,
    "estimated_difficulty": "easy",
    "cognitive_level": "application",
    "exemplar_ids_compared": [
      "cuet2024-economics-bookA-q2",
      "cuet2024-economics-bookA-q46"
    ]
  },
  "option_resolution": [
    {
      "option": "A",
      "status": "supported",
      "false_part": "",
      "premise_source": "arithmetic",
      "evidence_id": "",
      "premise_quote": "depositing it in bank-1 at 10 per cent interest per year",
      "reason": "10% of Rs 2,00,000 is Rs 20,000, which is the best forgone return."
    },
    {
      "option": "B",
      "status": "contradicted",
      "false_part": "Rs 10,000",
      "premise_source": "excerpt",
      "evidence_id": "E1.1",
      "premise_quote": "So the maximum benefit that you may get from other alternative activities is the interest from the bank-1.",
      "reason": "Opportunity cost reflects the maximum forgone benefit, not the lower 5% return."
    },
    {
      "option": "C",
      "status": "contradicted",
      "false_part": "Rs 30,000",
      "premise_source": "stem",
      "evidence_id": "",
      "premise_quote": "She can use the money in only one of these ways.",
      "reason": "Alternatives are mutually exclusive; their returns cannot be summed together."
    },
    {
      "option": "D",
      "status": "contradicted",
      "false_part": "Rs 0",
      "premise_source": "excerpt",
      "evidence_id": "E1.1",
      "premise_quote": "The opportunity cost of investing the money in your family business is therefore the amount of forgone interest from the bank-1.",
      "reason": "Opportunity cost is not the minimum return alternative."
    }
  ]
}
